target_customer: Adult children and caregivers buying a monitoring pendant for an elderly relative living at home
problem: Senior monitoring systems depended on a base station and left seniors unprotected outside the home. Amulyte made a mobile pendant with a help button, location and activity tracking.
business_model: Hardware at 99 dollars on preorder plus a 30 dollars per month subscription for cellular and the monitoring portal
product_category: Mobile personal emergency response and senior activity tracking

founders.name: Jaclyn Konzelmann
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (August 2013) says both founders are Waterloo alumni motivated by their grandparents.

competitors.name: BeClose
competitors.what: Virginia based in-home monitoring system for seniors

competitors.name: Lively
competitors.what: Activity sharing platform tracking objects around the house

technical_complexity.rationale: A pendant combining cellular, Wi-Fi positioning, GPS, an accelerometer and a week of battery life, with two way voice still in development, is hard hardware for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: No patents or data advantage are cited and incumbent personal emergency response firms could add mobile features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent acting against Amulyte. It went out of business without public explanation.

market_need_then: Seniors wanted to age at home and families worried about falls. A December 2013 report found funding for digital health startups targeting people over 50 rose from 413 million dollars in 2010 to 928 million in 2013.

branding.domain_note: Exact amulyte.com, which is now a parked domain listed as possibly for sale.

identity.visual_style: A pendant worn on the neck or kept in a pocket

branding.brand_signature: A single large help button pendant
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, MobiHealthNews and the YC blog; no sign of community.

brand_strength.rationale: The amulet like name fit a protective pendant but was easy to misspell, and the brand appears only in launch coverage.

outcome_analysis: Amulyte launched in August 2013 with a prototype pendant being tested at a local retirement home and consumer units promised for early 2014. It raised a small seed and a crowdfunding campaign, and directories say it went out of business around 2017. No company statement, post mortem or shipped unit count was found, so the cause is not public. The listed failure factors are inferences from the hardware difficulty and the lack of follow on funding.
notes: Seed figures: Seedtable says 255K in May 2013 and Dealroom says 260K; both are databases and the investors were not named, so Y Combinator is assumed only as the batch sponsor. The Wefunder crowdfunding in September 2013 and the 2017 out of business date rest on one directory (healthcarediscovery.ai, citing PitchBook); the amount is not public. exit.date is null because the shutdown date is unconfirmed. The site amulyte.com is a parked domain page.
